name: Synapse: Trajectory-as-Exemplar Prompting with Memory for Computer Control
venue: ICLR 2024 (The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations); also accepted at NeurIPS 2023 Foundation Models for Decision Making Workshop; preprint arXiv:2306.07863 (cs.AI), v1 Jun 2023 / v3 Jan 2024.
authors_affiliation: Longtao Zheng, Rundong Wang, Xinrun Wang, Bo An. All from Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore.
code_url: https://github.com/ltzheng/Synapse (project page: https://ltzheng.github.io/Synapse ; OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=Pc8AU1aF5e ; trajectories released on Google Drive).
task_domain: web / computer-control LLM agents: in-context-learning agents that perceive computer states (HTML of webpages) and emit keyboard/mouse actions to complete tasks; evaluated on GUI/web-navigation suites MiniWoB++ and Mind2Web.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent sequential decision-making for computer control. An LLM agent receives a natural-language task plus raw computer states (HTML), and outputs actions (code-style on MiniWoB++: click_xpath/type/press/click_option/move_mouse; CLICK/TYPE/SELECT on Mind2Web). The LLM is frozen and used purely via in-context learning (no gradient training). Supervision is a fixed offline pool of human demonstrations (MiniWoB++: demos for 48 of the tested 64 tasks; Mind2Web: the 1,009-task training set). MiniWoB++ is interactive/closed-environment with 50 episodes per task; Mind2Web is a static offline dataset scored against human-annotated ground truth across cross-task / cross-website / cross-domain generalization splits. No self-correction loop is used (unlike RCI/AdaPlanner). The exemplar memory is built once offline from the demo/training pool and is frozen at test time.
what_is_retrieved: demos / trajectories: complete demonstration trajectories (sequences of abstracted-state + action pairs) plus their associated state-abstraction prompts, retrieved as few-shot exemplars; keyed by task metadata embeddings.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic-style memory in form but functionally STATIC at deployment: the exemplar memory is an episodic store of demonstration trajectories that the agent constructs offline from the demonstration/training pool and then retrieves from; it does NOT grow during test-time deployment (no write-back of new trajectories). Effectively a static, offline-induced experience corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking by similarity (arg top-n over memory by Euclidean distance). On MiniWoB++ it retrieves the top-3 metadata matches then takes the most-common matched task and uses all of that task's exemplars (a small task-keyed set, ~3.45 exemplars/task avg). Not a completeness or precision-driven variable-size objective; selection size is largely fixed/budget-driven.
retrieval_unit: full trajectory: a complete demonstration trajectory expressed as <task, observation, action, ..., observation, action> over abstracted states, together with the matching state-abstraction prompt. The injected unit is a whole multi-step trajectory (case), not a single demo or step.
index_source: Static, offline-induced store. The memory D=(K,V) is built once by encoding all task metadata (K = embedding vectors) with their corresponding state-abstraction prompts and exemplary trajectories (V) from the human demonstration pool (MiniWoB++ 48 tasks) / Mind2Web training set (1,009 tasks). It is not grown at test time.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index: a fixed-size array of metadata embeddings stored in a vector database (Faiss), each metadata key mapped to its corresponding exemplars (state-abstraction prompts + trajectories). Metadata-keyed flat similarity index; no graph or learned hierarchy. (Implicit task-level grouping on MiniWoB++ via most-common-match heuristic.)
retriever_type: dense (off-the-shelf): embed task metadata with OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 and perform nearest-neighbor similarity search (Euclidean distance) over the Faiss vector index. No BM25, no learned/generative retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf). The embedding model (text-embedding-ada-002) is fixed/pretrained and not fine-tuned; retrieval is fixed top-n similarity over task-metadata embeddings with no contrastive/LM-feedback/RL training of the retriever.
query_construction: Intent/metadata extraction: the query key is the embedding of task metadata. On MiniWoB++ the metadata = task description concatenated with the initial state (from five random seeds of the 48 selected tasks); on Mind2Web the metadata = website name + domain + task description. Raw metadata is encoded directly (no synthetic query expansion or decomposition).
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at t=0): exemplars are retrieved once per task at the start, conditioned on the task metadata; the same retrieved exemplars are then reused across all steps of the episode (state abstraction itself is per-step but uses the already-retrieved prompts).
when_to_retrieve: one-shot: a single similarity-search retrieval is performed per task at the beginning; no iterative or uncertainty-triggered re-retrieval during the rollout.
retrieval_trigger_signal: fixed schedule: retrieval is triggered once, deterministically, when a new task arrives (Synapse first retrieves relevant exemplars from memory by similarity search before acting). No confidence/attention/learned-classifier/reflection trigger.
reranking: None (beyond the similarity top-n itself). On MiniWoB++ there is a lightweight majority-vote heuristic over the top-3 retrieved metadata matches (take the most common matched task, then use all its exemplars), but no cross-encoder or learned reranking stage.
retrieved_context_refinement: None at retrieval time. Retrieved trajectories are injected as few-shot exemplars largely verbatim. (Refinement happens at the STATE level, not the retrieval level: state abstraction filters task-irrelevant content from raw states before/within prompting, but it processes the current state, not the retrieved exemplars.)
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation: retrieved complete trajectories (plus their state-abstraction prompts) are placed into the LLM prompt as few-shot exemplars; the LLM is then prompted with these exemplary trajectories together with the current trajectory (task + previous observation-action pairs) to generate the next action (or temporally abstracted multi-action block).
planning_integration: one-shot exemplars at plan/act time with per-step interleaved acting: retrieved trajectory exemplars condition a closed-loop act loop. At each step the LLM (1) abstracts the raw state into a clean observation (few-shot, explicit <state,observation> or implicit <task,code>), then (2) given the exemplary trajectories + current history generates the next action(s); the action is executed, the new observation appended, and the loop continues until task completion or max steps. Trajectory-as-exemplar prompting lets the LLM emit temporally abstracted multi-action blocks (e.g., type(ls)+press(enter)) before querying a new state. No tree search / MCTS / self-correction.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-tool-call / per-action-block within a rollout: action generation is interleaved per environment step, but TaE prompting encourages temporally abstracted blocks of consecutive actions emitted between state queries (querying a new state only when necessary). Exemplar retrieval itself is per-task (per-answer), done once.
retrieved_item_representation: raw trajectory (state-abstracted): the injected exemplar is a free-text/code interleaved trajectory <task, observation, action, ...> where observations are the abstracted (cleaned) states and actions are code-style calls (agent.type(...), agent.click_xpath(...)) on MiniWoB++ or CLICK/TYPE/SELECT on Mind2Web. Not a distilled strategy or latent token; it is the demonstration trajectory itself.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: raw (state-abstracted) full trajectory / single demonstration of the matched task: the retrieved unit is a complete demonstration trajectory over abstracted states (a worked example), not a distilled strategy, guideline, skill, or workflow. State abstraction reduces per-state verbosity but the trajectory remains a concrete example.
noise_robustness_mechanism: (1) State abstraction filters task-irrelevant information from raw HTML states (explicit <state,observation> pairs, implicit <task,code> parsing, or zero-shot fallback if code errors), reducing distractor content and the 'lost-in-the-middle' long-context degradation; (2) code-style action grounding constrains generation; (3) the most-common-match retrieval heuristic on MiniWoB++ guards against a single mismatched metadata neighbor. No retriever-aware training or self-reflection relevance evaluator. A 2% failure on click-tab-2-hard is attributed to exemplar mismatch.
memory_type: episodic exemplar memory: a vector store D=(K,V) of demonstration-trajectory exemplars (with state-abstraction prompts) keyed by task-metadata embeddings; episodic/demonstration store rather than skill-library, workflow, procedural, graph, or latent memory.
write_back: No (effectively read-only at deployment). The memory is populated once offline from the human demonstration pool / Mind2Web training set; the agent does not write newly generated successful trajectories back into memory during test-time. (The paper notes future-work human-in-the-loop additions for customization, but no automatic online write-back is implemented.)
online_growth: No. The retrievable store is frozen after offline construction from the demonstration/training pool; it does not grow during deployment/test-time.
write_back_trigger: never (no online write-back). Memory is built offline by encoding all demonstration metadata and storing the corresponding exemplars; no per-episode success/failure/reflective write occurs at test time. Discussed as future work: combining the memory module with human intervention for user customization and task adaptation.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only / not stored as negative cases. Only successful human demonstration trajectories are stored as exemplars; failed trajectories are neither stored nor retrieved. Synapse explicitly avoids self-correction (unlike RCI/Reflexion/AdaPlanner), so it does not accumulate or reuse failure experiences. A text-transform failure case is analyzed qualitatively in the appendix but not fed back.
memory_evolution_update: append-only at construction time / static thereafter: all metadata-to-exemplar entries are written once during offline memory construction; stored entries are not merged, delta-updated, refined, pruned, or evolved during deployment.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Case/exemplar selection is fixed similarity top-n over frozen task-metadata embeddings (plus a deterministic majority-match heuristic on MiniWoB++); it is not an RL- or value-optimized retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private exemplar memory; no cross-agent or cross-framework experience sharing. (The prompting technique is described as broadly applicable/composable with other methods, but memory itself is not shared across agents.)
benchmarks: MiniWoB++ (legacy branch; 64 tested tasks, demos from 48 tasks, 16 unseen tasks; 50 episodes/task). Mind2Web (real-world web navigation; >2,000 tasks from 137 websites in 31 domains; training set 1,009 tasks/73 sites; test splits Cross-Task 252 tasks/69 sites, Cross-Website 177 tasks/10 sites, Cross-Domain 912 tasks/73 sites).
benchmark_family: web / GUI computer-control: MiniWoB++ (web GUI task suite) and Mind2Web (real-world web navigation; same family as Online-Mind2Web/WebArena).
baselines: MiniWoB++: RCI (ICL SOTA, recursive self-correction), AdaPlanner (concurrent, feedback self-correction), Pix2Act (concurrent, tree search + BC), CC-Net (BC+RL human-level, 2.4M demos), WebN-T5 and WebGUM (fine-tuned T5), plus the human-performance reference. Mind2Web: MindAct (MCQ-formatted ICL SOTA with element-ranking model), with both GPT-3.5 and CodeLlama-7B backbones. Backbone LLMs: gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 (MiniWoB++), gpt-3.5-turbo-16k-0613 (Mind2Web), CodeLlama-Instruct-7B; embeddings via text-embedding-ada-002; GPT-4 used to sample state-parsing code offline.
key_metrics: MiniWoB++: average task success rate (%). Mind2Web: Element selection accuracy (Ele. Acc), step success rate (Step SR), and whole-task success rate (SR) against human ground truth. Also reported: number of exemplars per task (data efficiency), recall of clean observations (target-element coverage).
headline_result: MiniWoB++: 99.2% average success rate across 64 tasks using demonstrations from only 48 tasks (a ~10% relative improvement; first ICL method to reach human-level performance and the first ICL method to solve book-flight), without self-correction. Mind2Web: 56% relative improvement in average step success rate over MindAct (the prior SOTA ICL prompting scheme) on GPT-3.5 across three generalization levels; ~2.5x step success rate over MindAct with CodeLlama-7B.
ablations: Incremental Mind2Web ablation (Table 1, both CodeLlama-7B and GPT-3.5) adding components one at a time: (a) state abstraction alone (direct generation with top-5 elements) beats MCQ-with-top-50 MindAct by 32% avg Step SR (e.g., GPT-3.5 Cross-Task Step SR 17.4 -> 25.2); (b) + TaE prompting adds +19% (to 50% over MindAct; Cross-Task Step SR -> 29.2); (c) + exemplar memory reaches 56% over MindAct (Cross-Task Step SR -> 30.6). Memory helps cross-task/cross-website but is marginal cross-domain (unseen domains -> larger retrieval distance, Table 2). MiniWoB++ ablations: state abstraction enables complex-state tasks (book-flight) and lifts email-inbox-nl-turk 52% -> 100%; TaE prompting fixes long-horizon/repeated-action tasks (guess-number 20%->100%, use-spinner 88%->100%, use-autocomplete 58%->98% vs RCI); exemplar memory gives ~100% avg on the 16 unseen tasks. Reducing top-k elements drops recall 86% -> 53% yet improves Step SR. RCI loses ~50% success rate if any of its three self-correction stages is removed.
evaluation_decoupling: Partially. Mind2Web reports element selection accuracy (Ele. Acc) and the recall of clean observations (86% at k=50 vs 53% at k=5) as intrinsic-style measures alongside end-to-end Step SR / SR, and reports retrieval-distance (similarity) statistics across test splits (Table 2). No standard ranked-retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) of the exemplar retriever itself are reported separately; retrieval quality is assessed mainly via downstream task gains.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. MiniWoB++ uses outcome (task success rate); Mind2Web adds intermediate process metrics: per-step Step SR and per-action Element Accuracy in addition to whole-task SR, giving step-wise process quality beyond final outcome.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency is a central motivation. State abstraction shrinks per-state tokens, enabling more exemplars within context. TaE prompting produces temporally abstracted multi-action blocks, reducing the number of LLM queries -> lower latency and cost (and higher long-horizon success). Sample efficiency: 64 tasks solved with demos from only 48 tasks; avg exemplars/task 3.45 (Synapse) vs 1.52 (RCI), vs CC-Net's 2.4M demos / WebGUM's 346,827 demos. Faiss used for efficient large-scale similarity search. Stated limitation: high inference latency due to LLM use (proposed remedy: distill a task-specific agent).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Budget-driven, mostly fixed small k. MiniWoB++: retrieve top-3 metadata matches then use all exemplars of the most-common matched task (avg 3.45 exemplars/task; up to 5 for hard tasks like book-flight). Mind2Web: retrieve exemplars of matched metadata; element budget set to k=3 for memory trajectories and previous observations and k=5 for the current observation (vs MindAct's k=50), deliberately trading recall (86%->53%) for shorter context and higher Step SR. Greedy decoding (temperature 0).
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes (similarity search over trajectory memory), Reuse: yes (trajectories injected as few-shot exemplars), Revise: no (no case adaptation/self-correction; exemplars used largely verbatim), Retain: no (no online write-back of new cases)]. Implements the Retrieve+Reuse half of the CBR cycle only.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it presents trajectory-as-exemplar prompting + exemplar memory under in-context-learning / retrieval-augmented prompting terminology. It nonetheless realizes CBR-style Retrieve+Reuse over full-trajectory cases.
index_content_separation: Partial: the index stores lightweight task-metadata embeddings (K) separated from the heavier content (V = state-abstraction prompts + full trajectories) loaded on retrieval. This is a metadata-key vs content separation rather than a progressive-disclosure SOP-index-then-content scheme.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (not a tool-retrieval method; environment interaction is via MiniWoB++/Mind2Web action APIs and code execution, not a live tool index/MCP).
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar: retrieved trajectory cases are reused as few-shot exemplars without explicit adaptation/revision (no LLM-prompted case rewriting, no execution-feedback revision, no critic). Generalization to novel tasks relies on the LLM implicitly adapting similar retrieved trajectories rather than an explicit Revise step.
builds_on: RCI (Kim et al., 2023; high-level-plan ICL computer agent, recursive self-correction), MindAct/Mind2Web (Deng et al., 2023; MCQ + element-ranking model), ReAct (Yao et al., 2022a), Code-as-Policies / ProgPrompt (code-as-action grounding), Chain-of-Thought / least-to-most prompting, in-context learning (Brown et al., 2020), Faiss (Johnson et al., 2019) for similarity search, OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002; concurrent skill-memory work Voyager (skill library) cited as complementary.
contrasts_with: RCI and AdaPlanner (self-correction-based ICL agents that rely on task-specific exemplars and recursive correction; Synapse drops self-correction and uses task-similarity memory), MindAct (MCQ-formatted step-wise prompting with top-50 elements; Synapse uses trajectory-as-exemplar direct generation with aggressive state abstraction), CC-Net / WebN-T5 / WebGUM / Pix2Act (BC+RL or fine-tuning on huge demonstration datasets; Synapse is data-efficient ICL), and prior agents that hard-code the task->exemplar mapping (Synapse retrieves exemplars from memory).
lineage: Group D (case-based planning): a trajectory-as-exemplar, retrieval-augmented computer-control agent that stores abstracted full-trajectory cases in an episodic memory and retrieves them as few-shot prompts, in the lineage of ICL web/computer agents (ReAct -> RCI/MindAct -> Synapse) and adjacent to skill-/experience-memory agents (Voyager, AdaPlanner). Realizes CBR Retrieve+Reuse over trajectory cases without explicit Revise/Retain.
